plans.headline: Discovery Drop-In & Storytime at Sarah P. Duke Gardens

main.why: The Charlotte Brody Discovery Garden hosts story times at 10:30 and self-guided discovery activities all morning — a beautiful outdoor setting for a 4-year-old to explore nature and hear stories.
tips: Arrive early to wander the paths before the first story time at 10:30.
Bring a snack and a water bottle; the gardens are free to enter.
Give a five-minute heads-up before leaving to make the transition to the car easier.

alternatives.why: Kids Discover Nature: Fall Leaves Fall at Harris Lake County Park is a free outdoor program with a picture-book read-aloud, a short hike and a leaf craft — a perfect autumn morning for a 4-year-old.
tips: Registration is required; sign up ahead.
Dress for a short hike and bring a water bottle.
Leave straight after the program to be home for lunch and the nap.

source.title: Kids Discover Nature: Fall Leaves Fall
source.address: 2112 County Park Dr., New Hill, NC  27562

alternatives.why: The Public Library Pop-Up brings story time to Gipson Play Plaza at Dix Park — books and stories on one of Raleigh's biggest playgrounds.
tips: Come any time during the drop-in window; the plaza is large so there is always room.
Bring a snack and sunscreen.
If rain arrives, head to a nearby library branch for storytime instead.

alternatives.why: Birdwatching for Beginners at Prairie Ridge is a calm outdoor science session at a working ecostation — a focused morning watching real birds in nature.
tips: Dress in muted colours so birds are not startled.
Bring binoculars if you have them; leaders often have extras.
Leave at noon to be home for lunch and the nap.

tips: No registration needed; arrive a few minutes early for a good spot.
The bilingual format is fun even if your family does not speak Spanish.
The park visit is weather-permitting; skip it if it is wet and head home.

plans.headline: Colorful Leaves at Hemlock Bluffs Nature Preserve, then Jack Smith Park

main.why: Colorful Leaves is a guided outdoor preschool nature session at Hemlock Bluffs where you and your child explore autumn together. Jack Smith Park is a short drive after for more fresh air and playground time.
tips: Registration and a small fee are required; book ahead.
Wear sturdy shoes suitable for light outdoor exploring.
The park visit is weather-permitting; pack a raincoat just in case.

alternatives.why: A full morning and early afternoon in the Charlotte Brody Discovery Garden: Discovery Drop-In stories and activities from 10:00, then Meet the Keepers at 13:00 to meet the bees, chickens and edible plants.
tips: Pack a lunch to eat in the gardens during the 12:00–13:00 gap between programs.
Both programs are free with no registration needed.
Let your child lead the pace through the garden paths.
